key_sub: Hypotenuse: square, add, square root. Shorter side: square, subtract, square root.
body_html:
How it works

In a right-angled triangle, the longest side (opposite the right angle) is the hypotenuse, c. Pythagoras' theorem: a² + b² = c².

  • To find the hypotenuse: square, add, square root.
  • To find a shorter side: square, subtract, square root.
Example

Find c in the triangle above.

c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100.

c = √100.

Answer: 10 cm

Example

The hypotenuse is 13 cm and one side is 5 cm. Find the other side.

13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144.

√144 = 12.

Answer: 12 cm

Common mistakes

  • Adding the sides without squaring: 3, 4 gives 5, not 7.
  • Forgetting the square root at the end.
  • Adding when you need a shorter side. Subtract from the hypotenuse squared.
  • Using a shorter side as the hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle.

faq.a: In a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse and a and b are the two shorter sides.

faq.q: How do I find a shorter side?
faq.a: Square the hypotenuse, subtract the square of the known side, then take the square root.

faq.q: How do I know which side is the hypotenuse?
faq.a: It is the longest side, opposite the right angle.

faq.q: How do I check if a triangle is right-angled?
faq.a: Square the two shorter sides and add. If the total equals the square of the longest side, it is right-angled.
